newsitem.title: UK: UK March new car registrations drop 0.23 percent.
newsitem.headline: UK March new car registrations drop 0.23 percent.

text.p: New car registrations in Britain dropped to 179,863 in March, down 0.23 percent on the year-earlier month, the Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders Ltd said on Monday.
The SMMT said registrations in the first quarter totalled 549,534, up 3.48 percent from the year-earlier quarter.

The group said imports accounted for 62.29 percent of the British market in March, up from 61.05 percent a year earlier. In the first quarter, imports took 65.36 percent of the market, up from 61.40 percent.
The society warned that market growth had slowed "dramatically" in the last two months.
"Of the 18,500 additional sales made in the first quarter, 15,000 were made in January," SMMT chief executive Ernie Thompson said in a statement.
In March and the year to date, private car sales took 43 percent of the market, unchanged from a year earlier.
